subject: Urgent: Veridian hosted API p99 spike after model v3.2 rollout
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridianhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Veridian Eng Ops <eng-ops@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2029-03-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API: sudden latency spike (p99) after model update

Hi Logan,

We just saw a sharp increase in our p99 latency for the Redwood hosted endpoint serving our clinical summarization flow. This started about 07:50 PDT after the model variant rolled to v3.2. P95 has crept up ~40% and p99 is ~2.5x normal. Impact: timeouts in our UI and a backlog of requests.

Attached a short screen grab and our internal trace IDs. Can you confirm whether any rollout touched our tenant and whether you can roll traffic back immediately? We're seeing increased error rates (5xx) on ~1% of requests, which is unusual.

This is customer-facing and causing our clinical ops to stall. Please escalate and advise ETA.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Dir, Platform Engineering
Veridian Health

Attachments:
- veridian_latency_chart_q1.png (image/png)
- mimicked-screenshots.zip (archive)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-21T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sudden latency spike (p99) after model update

Ellen — thanks for the quick flag and the traces. We're investigating. I see Veridian traffic did flip to model v3.2 in the hosted catalog at ~07:45 PDT as part of a wider variant rollout with traffic split rules. I am escalating now to eng and product.

Immediate actions I'm pushing for:
- Karthik to look at traces and KV cache behavior for v3.2 for high-seq requests
- Hold/roll back Veridian traffic to v3.1 if we confirm regression
- Monitor p95/p99 and 5xx closely; I will send updates every 30m until stable

Would you be able to confirm a couple of sample request IDs to correlate? If rollback is needed we will do it under your account and keep you posted.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Manager, Account Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-21T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Veridian outage risk — need quick credit & exec path

Heads up — Veridian (DEAL-VER-3491) has a p99 spike after v3.2 rollout. Customer is escalated to their platform lead. Potential commercial risk: enterprise clinical workflow impacted during weekday hours.

Ask: can we approve a customer goodwill credit up to $10k quickly if rollback is required? Also please loop in customer success & legal for any contract language changes if they request an SLA amendment. I'm on the call with Logan and customer.

Ben
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-21T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API: sudden latency spike (p99) after model update — quick triage

Short technical readout: I pulled the request traces Logan attached. Observations:
- v3.2 introduces longer average decode steps for sequences >600 tokens; we also see a KV cache key mismatch for a small subset of batched requests (likely due to a minor change in tokenizer behavior).
- This causes increased per-request compute and CPU fallback on our autoscaler edges for ~3.2% of traffic, which explains a 2–3x p99 increase while p95 moves moderately.
- Error mode: transient 5xx from worker timeouts when falling back to CPU execution.

Immediate mitigation proposed (low blast radius):
1) Roll Veridian back to pinned v3.1 for all traffic (we can do this at routing layer in ~7 minutes).
2) Apply a temporary throttle / split: send 75% traffic to v3.1, 25% to v3.2 for 1 hour with tracing enabled to capture failing keys.
3) Patch idea: align tokenizer canonicalization in v3.2's preprocessing (nontrivial — needs PR + canary).

I will prepare a one-page incident brief and attach sample request IDs. If Logan approves, I will execute rollback and run a parallel canary with throttling.

— Karthik
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments:
- veridian_request_form.pdf (text/pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Veridian Eng Ops <eng-ops@veridianhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-03-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sudden latency spike (p99) after model update

Ellen — quick update and mitigation steps we've enacted:
- We rolled Veridian traffic back to v3.1 at 08:58 PDT for all hosted API traffic and removed the v3.2 variant from your routing rule.
- Karthik has enabled throttled canary tracing (25% traffic) to capture failing tokenization cases; no customer-visible traffic remains on v3.2 unless you opt in.
- We are monitoring p95/p99 and 5xx now with a 1m dashboard; initial trends look improved but we'll keep this open.

Next steps: if you confirm back to normal on your side, we'll keep the rollback in place and schedule a controlled revalidation of v3.2 with your team during a low-traffic window. If you prefer a hotfix in v3.2 first, we can prioritize the tokenizer canonicalization patch.

I appreciate the quick context. Apologies for the disruption — we'll cover operational costs for the window and are prepared to offer account credit for the impact. Ben — please advise the commercial remedy and loop legal for any SLA discusion.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Manager, Account Solutions
Redwood Inference
